title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Grand Rapids, MI: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Grand Rapids furniture, automotive, packaging equipment and MDOT bridge welding: Part C choice, Part B travel, eligibility.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Grand Rapids: Six Days for West Michigan Furniture, Automotive, Equipment and Bridge Welding Inspectors
html:
Grand Rapids made its name on furniture, and West Michigan still builds a great deal of it, along with parts for the auto industry, packaging and food-line machinery, and the steel for the region's roads and buildings. Much of that welding happens on production lines at high volume, where a small drift in fillet size or an unnoticed undercut can turn into thousands of suspect parts. Plants that weld at that rate need people who can judge welds against a standard and explain the judgment, and the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) credential is how many of them show it. In Michigan the CWI also has a defined job inside the state transportation department's welder certification program.

The six-day Atlantis NDT course prepares West Michigan candidates for the CWI examination. It suits production welders and weld technicians, quality and supplier quality staff, robot programmers who own weld cells, NDT technicians and manufacturing engineers. AWS sets the examination, runs it and certifies those who pass, and every candidate applies to AWS personally and has to meet its eligibility and vision requirements. The course is not endorsed or approved by AWS, and no one at Atlantis has seen the examination. There is no Atlantis classroom in Grand Rapids. You can take the six days online at your own pace and put questions to an instructor, have your employer bring them to its plant for a group, or book one-to-one sessions online or in person at a place agreed when booking. The day-by-day outline is on the national CWI exam prep page.

Office furniture, battery trays and packaging lines

Steelcase is still headquartered in Grand Rapids, now as a subsidiary of HNI, which closed its acquisition of the company on December 10, 2025; before the deal, Steelcase reported about 11,300 employees worldwide. MillerKnoll, formed from Herman Miller and Knoll, lists West Michigan manufacturing plants in Zeeland, Holland and Spring Lake among its 13 plants. Steel frames, bases and brackets for desks, seating and storage are welded throughout these supply chains, often in robotic cells, and are inspected against the drawing and the company's own weld standard.

Automotive work is spread across the metro's suppliers. Benteler announced in December 2024 a 315,000-square-foot plant on the Site 36 property in Wyoming, Michigan, to make battery trays and other metal components for a US automaker's electric vehicles, with production planned to start in 2026 and 147 jobs. On the machinery side, SKA Fabricating in Grand Rapids builds depalletizers, palletizers, baggers and other container handling equipment for packaging lines, the kind of equipment where welds have to be sound, clean and consistent from one unit to the next.

MDOT's welder certification program puts a CWI in the test booth

The Michigan Department of Transportation runs a Welder Certification Program, managed by its Structural Fabrication Unit, that lets approved private testing agencies certify welders for MDOT work. The program document requires each agency to have a Certified Welding Inspector on staff to witness the entire welding operation; the CWI also performs the required mechanical testing and signs the test report. Testing follows AWS D1.1 as MDOT applies it, modified by MDOT's frequently used special provision 20SP-707A, and agencies may not pass any part of the testing to a third party without the Structural Fabrication Engineer's approval.

That makes the CWI a working credential for testing laboratories and inspection agencies in West Michigan, not just a line on a résumé. A Grand Rapids CWI who wants to examine welders for MDOT work needs to know the D1.1 qualification clauses thoroughly, which is one more reason to consider D1.1 for Part C.

Steel repairs and a century-old bridge on US-131

MDOT's 2026 work in Grand Rapids included two bridge jobs on US-131. The Martin Luther King Jr. Street bridge over the freeway, a section first built in the 1920s to span railroad tracks, closed from March 2, 2026 for replacement, with completion estimated for mid-November. From September 8, crews worked on the southbound US-131 bridge over northbound US-131, a job MDOT described as substructure improvements, steel beam repair, barrier wall reconstruction and approach work, estimated to finish in late October.

MDOT's construction manual for structural steel says field welding follows the current AWS D1.5 Bridge Welding Code under an AASHTO/AWS D1.5 field welding plan, Form 0395, approved by the Structural Fabrication Unit. Welders on MDOT work must be endorsed through the department's welder qualification or certification program, and nondestructive testing of welds is done by personnel qualified as ASNT Level II or Level III under SNT-TC-1A. A candidate who expects to inspect repair welding on state bridges should look hard at D1.5 for Part C. Background: AWS D1.5.

Inspecting production welds at volume

Most CWI study material is written around structural fabrication, yet much of West Michigan's welding is production work: robotic gas metal arc welding on sheet and light plate, fixtures that set the fit-up, and parts made by the thousand. Three habits from the CWI syllabus carry straight into that setting. Measure rather than eyeball: fillet gauge readings recorded at the start, middle and end of a run catch a drifting torch angle long before visual impressions do. Read the weld symbols on the drawing literally, including length and pitch on intermittent welds, because a robot program can be right on the arrow side and missing on the other side. And know how the common discontinuities form, since porosity from contaminated parts, undercut from excessive travel speed and incomplete fusion at cold starts each point to a different correction.

Resistance spot welds and brazed joints are common in automotive and furniture assemblies. Where an automotive customer calls it up, arc-welded steel parts can be accepted to AWS D8.8M:2021, Specification for Automotive Weld Quality: Arc Welding of Steel, and spot welds to AWS D8.1M; neither D8 document is a Part C option. A plant should therefore teach its own acceptance standard alongside the CWI material, which concentrates on what the examination covers: processes and terminology, symbols, metallurgy, testing, measurement and code application.

Stainless, aluminum and the codes that are not on the list

Food and packaging machinery uses a lot of stainless steel, and some of the metro's automotive and furniture work is in aluminum. Two points matter for Part C. AWS D1.2, the structural aluminum code, is on the AWS list of code books in its 2014 edition, so an aluminum fabricator's inspector has a code that matches the work. AWS D1.6, the stainless steel structural welding code, is not on the list, so a candidate from a stainless shop normally picks D1.1 or the ASME option and learns the stainless differences on the job.

The full list in November 2026 was AWS D1.1:2020, API 1104 in its 22nd edition, AWS D1.2:2014, AWS D1.5:2020 with Clause 12, AWS D15.1:2019, AWS D17.1:2024, the ASME option of Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, and an ISO option. Buy the edition AWS names, which can be older than the latest one in print. Related reading: AWS D1.1 and WPS, PQR and WPQ explained.

Choosing Part C in West Michigan: four short answers

  • Steel furniture, automotive structures, general fabrication or MDOT welder testing: AWS D1.1. It is the structural steel code and the basis of the MDOT testing program.
  • Bridge steel and highway structures: AWS D1.5, which MDOT applies to field welding on its bridges and which has its own fracture-critical clause.
  • Aluminum frames, trailers or enclosures: AWS D1.2, if aluminum is genuinely most of what you inspect.
  • Plant utilities, boilers and process piping at a food, beverage or chemical plant: the ASME option, because those systems are qualified to Section IX and built to B31.1 or B31.3.

If you are torn between two, choose the one you will keep using after the exam. Part C rewards knowing where things are in the book, and that familiarity keeps paying off at work.

GRCC, M-TEC and the West Michigan Section

Grand Rapids Community College runs its Welding/Fabrication Technician program at the Leslie E. Tassell M-TEC on Godfrey Avenue SW: 612 clock hours over about 20 weeks, Monday through Thursday in the daytime, covering cutting, brazing and welding of metal components, with MIG and TIG work on aluminum and stainless steel, metallurgy, blueprint reading and shop math. GRCC says credits from the certificate may apply toward its welding technology associate degree. Graduates who go into the trade should keep a log of every job from the start, because beyond the education credit AWS counts verifiable work, not course hours.

The AWS West Michigan Section, in District 11, raises money for its scholarship program through an annual golf outing, held on June 10 in 2026. AWS lists five other sections in District 11 across Michigan and northwest Ohio, among them Detroit, Central Michigan and Saginaw Valley. Section meetings and events are where you meet CWIs who have taken the exam recently and hear which employers are hiring inspectors.

Part B from Grand Rapids

Parts A and C are computer-based tests that AWS delivers at Prometric centers, so they can be taken close to home once AWS issues your eligibility code. Part B, the practical, is given only at AWS educational seminar locations. On the November 2026 AWS list, Detroit was the only Michigan location, and Chicago, Milwaukee, Indianapolis and Cleveland were the other listed sites around the Great Lakes. The Hobart Institute of Welding Technology in Troy, Ohio, also publishes its 2026 CWI sessions with AWS exam site codes; check with AWS which of them accept candidates who are not enrolled in that course.

In the US, AWS closes applications for a Part B date six weeks before it. Apply once your vision record and experience evidence are complete, then book travel and leave yourself room for a retake, since AWS requires 72 percent on each part. Use the CWI budget calculator to add travel and days away from work.

Documenting a production career for AWS

Many West Michigan candidates have spent years in production cells rather than on job sites, and AWS can accept that work if it is welding-related and verifiable. Describe it in terms AWS can assess: the processes and materials, whether you set up and adjusted welding equipment, whether you checked parts against drawings or a weld standard, whether you dispositioned rejects or trained other operators. Name a supervisor or quality manager who can confirm each period.

Consider a hypothetical robot technician with an associate degree in engineering technology who has spent three years programming and maintaining weld cells for a furniture maker, checking first parts against drawings and adjusting parameters when gauging showed undersized fillets. With that degree AWS asks for two years of welding-related experience, so the question is not the length of the record but whether AWS accepts programming and process work as welding-related. Describe the welding content of the job plainly and let AWS decide.

AWS ties the experience requirement to education: one year after a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology, rising through two, three and four years to five for a high school diploma or equivalent, and longer with less schooling. The vision test is recorded on AWS's visual acuity form and has to be current on exam day. The CWI requirements guide has the details.

Running the six days at a West Michigan plant

For a manufacturer preparing a group, the corporate format brings the course to the plant. The practical work can use the plant's own parts and rejects, from furniture bases to brackets and frames, measured with the plant's gauges and judged against its weld standard as well as the code. Code exercises can run in D1.1 for steel work, D1.2 where the plant welds aluminum, or the ASME option for maintenance and piping staff. The plant picks the weeks, so the course can fit between a model changeover and a busy quarter.

Group delivery does not change who holds the certificate. Every participant applies to AWS individually, provides their own experience evidence and vision record, and takes all three parts in their own name.

After the CWI in Grand Rapids

A new CWI might take over weld audits and supplier quality checks in a furniture or automotive plant, examine welders for a testing agency working under the MDOT program, or inspect structural steel on building projects. Those who also want to perform NDT need method training and employer certification under a written practice. Atlantis runs training based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, such as VT Level 2, PT Level 2 for stainless and aluminum parts and MT Level 2, and the employer certifies the technician. The CWI is renewed every three years and recertified at nine through one of the routes AWS sets.

Local and nearby pages: NDT training in Grand Rapids, ultrasonic testing in Grand Rapids, magnetic particle testing in Grand Rapids, Practical NDT in Grand Rapids, NDT training in Michigan and CWI exam prep in Detroit and Chicago.

Sending a Grand Rapids enquiry

Let us know how many candidates there are, which format suits them, the Part C code book each expects to use and roughly when they hope to sit the exam. For a plant group, include the address and the weeks that work around production. If you are not sure the experience will satisfy AWS, summarize it and we will tell you what to confirm with AWS first. Fees for your format are quoted on request, and our reply comes within one business day.

faq.q: Is there an AWS section in Grand Rapids?
faq.a: Yes. The AWS West Michigan Section is part of District 11 and funds scholarships through an annual golf outing, held on June 10 in 2026. The Detroit, Central Michigan and Saginaw Valley sections are also in District 11.

faq.q: Does MDOT require a CWI to test welders?
faq.a: Under MDOT's Welder Certification Program, each approved private testing agency must have a Certified Welding Inspector on staff to witness the entire welding operation, perform the mechanical testing and sign the test report. Testing follows AWS D1.1 as modified by MDOT.

faq.q: Where do West Michigan candidates take Part B?
faq.a: At an AWS seminar location. In November 2026 Detroit was the only listed site in Michigan, with Chicago, Milwaukee, Indianapolis and Cleveland nearby on the list. Parts A and C are computer-based at Prometric centers.

faq.q: Can I choose AWS D1.6 for Part C?
faq.a: No. AWS D1.6, the stainless steel structural code, is not on the AWS list of Part C code books. Stainless shop candidates usually choose AWS D1.1 or the ASME option.

faq.q: Which code should a furniture or automotive plant inspector choose?
faq.a: AWS D1.1 for steel work in most cases, or AWS D1.2 if the plant mainly welds aluminum. Resistance spot welds and brazed joints are normally inspected to the customer's own standard.

faq.q: Does the GRCC welding program reduce the experience I need?
faq.a: AWS lists four years of welding-related experience for candidates who completed trade or vocational courses, and AWS decides whether a program and your work qualify. Keep a record of every job from the start.

faq.q: Can our plant host the six days?
faq.a: Yes. The corporate format brings the six days to your facility for a group, using your parts, gauges and weld standard. Each participant applies to AWS individually.

faq.q: Is the course endorsed by AWS?
faq.a: No. AWS has not approved or endorsed the course and Atlantis has no access to the examination. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in Grand Rapids?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Grand Rapids. You study online, at your employer's site with a group, or one-to-one online or in person at a location agreed when booking. Atlantis offices are in Houston and Hyderabad.

faq.q: How do I request a quote?
faq.a: Send the enquiry from this page with the number of candidates, the format and the Part C code each expects to use. We give a quote for that format and answer within one business day.
